'''Brandon Simone Armstrong''' (born June 16, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Born in [[San Francisco, California]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine Waves]] and was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 23rd overall pick of the [[2001 NBA draft]]. He was traded to the [[New Jersey Nets]], where he played three seasons in the [[NBA]]. He later played in Italy, Spain, Poland and Ukraine, and spent a season in the [[NBA D-League]].

==Professional career==
Armstrong was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 23rd overall pick of the [[2001 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/history/draft/2001-draft/|title=NBA Draft history: 2001 Draft|work=NBA.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150330113217/http://www.nba.com/history/draft/2001-draft/|archive-date=March 30, 2015}}</ref> He was traded along with fellow Rockets draft picks [[Richard Jefferson]] and [[Jason Collins]] to the [[New Jersey Nets]] in exchange for the draft rights to New Jersey's [[Eddie Griffin (basketball)|Eddie Griffin]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rajan|first=Greg|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/rockets/article/Eddie-Griffin-Rockets-2001-lottery-Richard-16249909.php|title=Rockets in the lottery: All-in on Eddie Griffin in 2001|work=houstonchronicle.com|date=June 16, 2021|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref> In three seasons with the Nets, Armstrong averaged 2.2 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/armstbr01.html|title=Brandon Armstrong|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref> He only played 17 games in [[2002–03 New Jersey Nets season|2002–03]] due to suffering from regular back pain. He was subsequently not on the 2003 playoff roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/brandon_armstrong/bio.html|title=Brandon Armstrong|work=NBA.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114051142/http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/brandon_armstrong/bio.html|archive-date=November 14, 2012}}</ref>

Armstrong became a free agent in 2004 and signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]], but was waived prior to the start of the [[2004–05 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Brandon-Armstrong/Summary/508|title=Brandon Armstrong|work=realgm.com|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref> Armstrong's final NBA game was played in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semi-Finals on May 20, 2004. In that game, the Nets would drop the series to the Detroit Pistons by losing the game 69 - 90. Armstrong played for 4 minutes and the only stat he recorded was 1 assist.

For the 2005–06 season, Armstrong moved to Italy to play for [[Roseto Basket]]. He left the team in November 2005 after appearing in seven games.<ref name=latinbasket>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.latinbasket.com/player/Brandon-Armstrong/Venezuela/Marinos-de-Anzoategui/30227|title=Brandon Armstrong|work=latinbasket.com|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref> In February 2006, he moved to Spain and played 10 games for Calpe Aguas.<ref name="latinbasket" />

On November 2, 2006, Armstorng was selected by the [[Dakota Wizards]] in the third round of the [[2006 NBA Development League draft|NBA Development League draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/2006-nba-development-league-draft-concludes/n-3392016|title=2006 NBA Development League Draft concludes|work=oursportscentral.com|date=November 2, 2006|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref> He was waived by the Wizards on January 20, 2007.<ref name=transactions0607>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html|title=2006-07 Transactions|work=NBA.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160116141624/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html|archive-date=January 16, 2016}}</ref> He was acquired by the [[Bakersfield Jam]] on February 8 but then waived on February 28.<ref name="transactions0607" /> He was then acquired by the [[Anaheim Arsenal]] on March 15 but then waived again on March 26.<ref name="transactions0607" />

For the 2007–08 season, Armstrong moved to Poland to play for [[SKK Kotwica Kołobrzeg|Kotwica Kołobrzeg]]. In 26 games, he averaged 11.2 points per game.<ref name="latinbasket" />

For the 2008–09 season, Armstrong moved to Ukraine to play for [[BC Budivelnyk|Budivelnyk]]. His last game for Budivelnyk was on January 9, 2009.<ref name="latinbasket" />

In February 2009, Armstrong trialed with [[Marinos B.B.C.|Marinos de Anzoátegui]] of the Venezuelan [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]]. He was fighting for a position on the team with a fellow American Michael Gale,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://diarioeltiempo.wordpress.com/2009/02/17/melendez-estoy-contento-con-actitud-de-los-jugadores/|title=Meléndez: Estoy contento con actitud de los jugadores|work=diarioeltiempo.wordpress.com|date=February 17, 2009|access-date=December 31, 2021|language=Spanish}}</ref> but he ultimately did not make the team and did not debut for Marinos.<ref name="latinbasket" />
